step_1.casting: Use case: product-mockup. Create one photorealistic editorial lifestyle photograph, portrait 1080 by 1565 proportion, no text or advertising overlay. Show a modern black Android smartphone with thin black bezel, subtle rounded screen corners, and a centered small punch-hole front camera. The screen is completely blank dark charcoal, since an authentic app screenshot will be inserted in a separate second step. The entire display is visible and unobstructed, photographed almost straight-on so its edges are nearly parallel to the image edges. Display has a realistic approximately 9:20 aspect ratio. Make the phone large enough for app text to be legible after insertion: roughly 60% of the image width and 86% of the image height. Keep the whole phone inside the image. Natural materials, believable object sizes and lighting, a calm cream and subdued teal atmosphere. No invented UI, letters, graphics on the screen, watermarks or captions. Scene: a real home desk or wooden table. The black phone sits upright on a discreet stand, slightly right of center. Beside it, clearly visible on the left, is a real Google Home smart speaker with its familiar white tapered upper body and light gray fabric lower base. A small portion of a laptop and paper notebook gives home desk context without obscuring the phone or speaker. Soft daylight, close product composition, realistic shadows, camera facing the phone squarely at screen height. The speaker is a prop showing compatible casting hardware; avoid displaying invented device states or indicator lights.

step_2_imagegen_preview.casting: Use case: compositing. Input image 1 is the edit target: a photorealistic phone scene with a blank dark screen. Input image 2 is the exact authentic Android app capture to insert. Perform only the second step: place image 2 inside the existing phone display in image 1, fitted to its screen corners and perspective. Preserve the surrounding photograph, device bezel, physical camera cutout, hands, furniture, speaker, lighting, and framing exactly. Keep the entire screenshot including its native status bar and gesture bar. Treat the screenshot as a fixed image decal, preserving its book artwork, text, controls, colors, icons, layout, timer selection, playback and volume state; do not reimagine or redraw app UI. No extra UI, no captions, no logos, no repeated floating screenshot beside the phone. Scale and align the screenshot to fill the actual physical phone screen, clipping only the tiny corners or camera hole occupied by the existing hardware. The result must look like this exact app running on this actual phone in the scene.
